name: XME.lol
tagline: A hosted one-page personal profile that collects your links, socials and contact details behind a short URL.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: A link-in-bio page is one of the smallest real products in software: a title, an avatar, a list of links, and a stylesheet. An agent can produce a static version in an afternoon, and a static file on a CDN will outlive most hosted profile services. The only genuinely annoying parts are the short memorable domain and the click analytics, and neither is technically hard, just mildly tedious. What you are actually paying for here is the convenience of editing from your phone and never thinking about deploys. Fair trade for some people, not a moat.
coreLoopDIY: Renders a static single-page profile from one JSON file: avatar, bio, link buttons with icons, social row, theme, and a generated OG image, deployable to any static host.
requirements: a domain, or acceptance of a free host subdomain
any static host such as Cloudflare Pages, Netlify or GitHub Pages
willingness to edit a JSON file and push to change your links
whatYouLose: A short catchy domain that fits in a bio field, which you now have to buy yourself
Click analytics per link, unless you bolt on a redirect worker and a counter
Editing from your phone in ten seconds without touching a repo
Prebuilt themes and layout polish that someone already A/B tested for you
Automatic link previews, favicon fetching and social metadata scraping
moatNotes: The real asset in this category is a short domain other people recognise, not the page renderer.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the page is not the work, the maintenance is. People pay so that updating a link is a text field on a phone instead of a commit, so the URL is short enough to say out loud, and so someone else owns the uptime when a recruiter or a client actually clicks through. A few dollars a month to never think about it again is a rational purchase even when the build is trivial, which is exactly why this category has forty competitors and no winner.
notes: The build is an afternoon; the short domain is the part you actually have to pay for.
prompt:
Build a static personal link-in-bio site in an empty folder.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Astro with TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, zero client JS frameworks.
- Output is a fully static site in dist/, no server, no database, no accounts.

Content model:
- One file, src/data/profile.json, holding: name, handle, tagline, avatar path, theme name, an array of links (label, url, optional icon slug, optional highlight boolean), and an array of socials (platform, url).
- Nothing else in the repo should need editing to change the page.

Page requirements:
- A single index page: avatar, name, handle, tagline, vertical stack of large tappable link buttons, then a compact social icon row at the bottom.
- Mobile first, tap targets at least 44px tall, works fine at 320px wide.
- Three themes selectable by string in profile.json: light, dark, and a high contrast neon. Respect prefers-color-scheme when theme is set to auto.
- Local SVG icon set checked into the repo. Do not fetch icons or fonts from a CDN at runtime.
- Generate an OG image at build time with satori and resvg-js from the profile data, plus correct title, description, og and twitter meta tags.
- Include a /robots.txt and a favicon generated from the avatar.

Explicitly out of scope: user accounts, an admin UI, a CMS, analytics, cookie banners, newsletter capture, telemetry of any kind.

Also deliver:
- npm run dev and npm run build working from a clean clone.
- A .env.example only if a build value is genuinely needed, otherwise no .env at all.
- A README with a five line quickstart and a one command deploy note for Cloudflare Pages.
- A basic Playwright test asserting every link in profile.json renders exactly once with the right href.
